children.title: Rational Responses to Epistemic Peer Disagreement

detail.title: Rational Responses to Epistemic Peer Disagreement
detail.summary: Epistemic disagreement occurs when agents with identical evidence reach different conclusions. The literature identifies three primary stances: the Conciliatory view, the Stubborn view, and the Non-Conciliatory view. These stances interact with Uniqueness and Permissivism; Uniqueness asserts that evidence dictates one correct rational attitude, whereas Permissivism allows for multiple. Current evidence suggests that unconditional deference (Conciliatory view) may be less tenable than a nuanced approach that accounts for case-specific conditions.
detail.reason: This notebook synthesizes the initial source material into a structured assessment of the project's core philosophical question.
